name: Ashmarked No-Brand Painted Manifesto Coat
description: A floor-length Shelf-made coat assembled from four or five different dead garments — the body from a decommissioned transit authority duster, sleeves from a cracked rubberized chem-jacket, hood from raw salvage felt. Every surface is hand-painted with white and rust-red industrial paint: anti-corponation slogans in a mix of Yoruba script, Tagalog, and phonetic English crowd the chest, while the back carries a massive mural of Meridian 88's skyline drowning beneath a stylized wave. No two coats are identical. The stitching is intentionally exposed, a deliberate anti-craft statement.
functionality: Rubberized sleeve panels provide functional acid rain resistance. Deep internal pockets are hand-stitched with reinforced canvas. The layered construction provides surprising warmth.
what_it_says: This person makes their politics visible and doesn't care who reads them.
worn_by: runners who want to disappear into crowds
price_range: Φ0–Φ30 in materials — traded or gifted within community
story_hooks: A specific coat is recognized by CorpSec intelligence as belonging to a protest organizer they've been trying to identify for months.
A Tier 4 fashion house has begun selling 'authentic Shelf manifesto coats' at Φ4,000 each — the original makers are furious and planning a response.
Hidden beneath the paint on one coat is a hand-drawn map of a Shelf infrastructure vulnerability that could be used for sabotage — or protection.
